notes: The fronted *hast* was given to the interrogative אִם under rules 20 and 50, leaving the possessive לְ of לָךְ `unrepresented`. Those two rules hand the particle a construction-supplied copula (*Is*, *Am*, *Art*, *Are*, *Was*) and an existential frame respectively — words no other morpheme licenses. A possessive *have* is neither: rule 43 assigns it to whatever makes the clause possessive, here the לְ of a verbless possessive clause, exactly as `לָהֶם מִסְגְּרוֹת` → *they had panels* puts *had* on לְ and the pronoun on the suffix. Rule 43's subtraction test settles it — drop *hast* and only the possession relation has gone unstated. Under the accepted reading the one morpheme that carries that relation held nothing at all, against rule 2. The question is marked by inversion of the possessive verb and no separate auxiliary is written, so the particle is `unrepresented` under rule 17's own inversion sentence. This does not disturb vv.2 and 8, where the fronted *Shall* and *Wilt* are auxiliaries that leave their verbs a rendering of their own, or the second clause here, which writes no particle at all.
